title: A Garden for the Postcard
premise: Theo Reyes, a pastry chef drowning in café debt, inherits half of a failing orchard in the coastal town of Merrow's Bend — the other half belongs to Juniper Hale, the estranged childhood friend whose family once destroyed his. The deed carries an old covenant: neither heir can sell unless both agree, and the bank holding Theo's café notes is circling, backed by a developer who wants the orchard razed. As Theo and Juniper restore the trees together, they uncover proof that the original deed transfer was forged — justice that exists nowhere in the law but in the town's own memory and ledgers. In the end, Theo walks away from a career-making offer in Paris, they expose the forgery at a public auction, save both orchard and café, and choose each other over every safe version of their lives.
about_author: Ansel Winterbourne is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing love letters he never sent from kitchens in three countries. He now lives above a bakery on the Oregon coast, where he tends four stubborn apple trees and insists fiction is just pastry with longer proofing times.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A brutal service night at his failing café ends with a final notice from the bank and a certified letter: he has inherited half of an orchard he didn't know existed. Emotional beat: exhaustion cracking open into disbelief — hope arriving disguised as paperwork.

chapters.title: The Other Name on the Deed
chapters.summary: Theo drives to Merrow's Bend and reads the deed twice: his name beside Juniper Hale's, the girl whose family bought out his grandfather's farm decades ago. He meets her at the property gate, armed and hostile. Beat: old wounds recognized across new ground.

chapters.title: Covenant of Two
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She explains the strange covenant — neither can sell without the other — and reveals the developer's offer she's been refusing for a year. Theo, needing money desperately, is tempted. Beat: two people discovering they are locked together by paper and resentment.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Walking the neglected rows, Theo finds his grandfather's initials carved into the oldest apple tree — and a grafting technique only his family used. The orchard was never truly the Hales'. Beat: inheritance as revelation rather than windfall.

chapters.title: The Paris Letter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. An offer arrives: head pastry chef at a celebrated Paris pâtisserie, starting in ten weeks — exactly when the bank's deadline falls. Selling his half would fund everything. Beat: duty and desire pulling in opposite directions before love even enters it.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A storm fells a limb onto the cottage roof; Theo shows up with tools and flour-dusted hands to help patch it. Working side by side, banter thaws into something warmer. Beat: first involuntary tenderness, immediately distrusted.

chapters.title: Ledgers in the Attic
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Searching the attic for the covenant's terms, they find Theo's grandfather's farm ledgers — and a 1974 deed transfer bearing a signature dated three days after the signer's death. Beat: suspicion hardening into evidence; the past becomes a case file.

chapters.title: The Developer's Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Victor Marsh, the developer, wines and dines Theo privately, offering to buy his half at triple value and quietly settle his café debt. Theo doesn't say no. Beat: temptation wearing a tailored suit; guilt carried home like contraband.

chapters.title: First Harvest Together
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Pressed apples into cider at dawn, flour on Theo's sleeves, laughter surprising them both. Juniper admits why she stayed: her father's deathbed confession about the forged deed. Beat: intimacy earned through shared labor and shared shame.

chapters.title: The Kiss at the Cider Press
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. After the press, in the amber light of the barn, they kiss — then Juniper pulls back, having seen Marsh's car pass earlier. 'Did you take his money?' she asks. Beat: joy interrupted by the question that will define everything.

chapters.title: Silence Between Rows
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Theo neither confirms nor denies the deal; Juniper withdraws, working the east field alone. Both throw themselves into restoration as avoidance. Beat: love against duty begins its real war — inside each of them.

chapters.title: The Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the diner, elderly neighbors confirm the 1974 story: Theo's grandfather was cheated, and half the town knew and said nothing. Shame ripples outward. Beat: justice outside the law requires witnesses, and witnesses require courage.

chapters.title: Marsh Tightens the Screws
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Marsh accelerates: the bank calls Theo's café note due in three weeks, and a county rezoning vote looms that would gut the orchard's value. Beat: the vise closing; time made visible and merciless.

chapters.title: What the Heart Is For
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo trains himself not to feel — early runs, double shifts, no calls to Juniper — proving his old thesis that the heart is a muscle like any other. It fails spectacularly. Beat: the blurb's thesis tested and broken.

chapters.title: The Found Signature
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. In the county archive, they find the notary's granddaughter, who kept her grandmother's journals: a full account of the coerced forgery. Proof enough for the town, if not yet for a court. Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo formally rejects Marsh's offer — forfeiting the money that could save his café — because selling stolen ground would make him complicit in the original theft. Beat: the choice between career and conscience made explicit, alone, at cost.

chapters.title: Betrayal Revealed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper learns Theo met Marsh twice and nearly sold — before he refused. Feeling deceived about the deception itself, she tells him the partnership, and whatever else, is over. Beat: the darkest hour; love wounded not by betrayal but by concealment.

chapters.title: Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Marsh posts the foreclosure auction: the orchard, in nine days, regardless of the covenant — he's found a procedural loophole. Theo realizes only public exposure of the forgery can stop it. Beat: stakes crystallized; the plan forms under pressure.

chapters.title: Rallying Merrow's Bend
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They reconcile over the ledgers spread across the café counter, then spend three days gathering testimony, photographs, and the notary's journal — the whole town choosing memory over money. Beat: forgiveness as collaboration; justice assembled by hand.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the courthouse steps, before bidding opens, Theo reads the grandfather's ledger aloud and presents the journal; the crowd refuses to bid, the notary's sworn statement goes to the county recorder, and Marsh's financing collapses. Beat: climax — justice outside the law, delivered publicly and irreversibly.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Rows
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Weeks later: the forgery voids the 1974 transfer, restoring clear title; the café survives on a renegotiated note; the Paris offer expires unanswered. They plant twenty-two new trees, one per chapter of what it took. Beat: resolution — everything saved except the safe life.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Postcard
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Epilogue in autumn: the orchard heavy with fruit, a postcard from Paris pinned to the barn wall, unsigned and unregretted. Theo finally admits the heart isn't containable — it's a garden, and this one is theirs. Beat: quiet, earned peace; love chosen daily.
